successors.name: Khwarazmian Empire
successors.text: Herat in 1206, Balkh soon after, and the Ghor remnant (Ghor, Bamiyan) outright in 1215: 'The Khwarezmians under Ala al-Din Muhammad captured Herat and Ghor in 1206'; 'Shah Muhammad II uprooted the…

successors.name: Mamluk dynasty of Delhi
successors.text: Lahore, Delhi, the Doab and Ajmer: Aibak, who 'became the sultan of Delhi, establishing the Mamluk dynasty' (Mamluk page)

successors.name: Yildiz of Ghazni
successors.text: Ghazni, Kabul and the south-east of Afghanistan of Cliopatria's 1206 shape

ledger.x: 1152: the Ghurids of Ghor, vassals of the Seljuks, appear in Cliopatria.
1162: the Nasrid dynasty of Sistan becomes a Ghurid vassal.
1173: Muhammad of Ghor is crowned at Ghazni and holds it as his seat; his brother Ghiyath al-Din returns to Firuzkuh.
1175: the Ghurids take Herat from the Seljuks.
1175: Muhammad takes Multan from the Qarmatians.

1176: Uch. 'also took Uch by 1176'; the Muhammad of Ghor page's infobox puts Uch in 1175 ('captured Multan and Uch from the Carmathians within a year') and its body after 1179. Coordinates approximate (Uch is not in the gazetteer).
1178: the Ghurid army marches on Gujarat and is routed at Kasahrada (Mount Abu).
1178: the Ghurid retreat from Mount Abu ends the first Gujarat campaign; the next attack on Gujarat is Aibak's of 1197.
1186: Lahore falls and the Ghaznavids end.
1190: the Ghurid generals take Bathinda and open the war with the Chahamanas.
1192: the Second Battle of Tarain ends the contest.
1192: Haryana passes to the Ghurids under Aibak.
1194: Muhammad crosses the Yamuna against the Gahadavalas.

c. 1196: Bayana and Thankar. 'Muhammad returned to the Indian frontier again around 1196'; Thankar's ruler Kumarpal was defeated and Bahauddin Tughril took control of Bayana (Gwalior fell to Tughril later, undated). Coordinates approximate (Bayana is not in the gazetteer).

ledger.cp: Balkh vassal (the page does not name the holder)

ledger.x: 1200: Muhammad and Ghiyath al-Din take Khorasan.

1200: Bihar. The Muhammad of Ghor page says only that his lieutenants, 'notably Bakhtiyar Khalji', extended influence east, with northern Bihar mentioned, and gives no date; 1200 is the year the sena-dynasty dossier (sa-03) records the loss of Bihar, and Cliopatria's 1202 shape reaches it. [Repair sa-04-a, thin…
1206: the Khwarazmians take Herat and Ghor.
1206: the Soomra vassalage lapses with Muhammad of Ghor's death.
1206 or soon after: Balkh passes to Khwarazm.
1206 (after the assassination of 15 March): the Ghurid sultans become Khwarazmian vassals.
1206: Aibak founds the Delhi Mamluk dynasty.
1212: the Nasrids of Sistan are Khwarazmian vassals (the same sentence).
1215: Muhammad II ends the Ghurid vassalage.

wars.name: Ghurid-Ghaznavid war and conquest of the Punjab
wars.outcome: Ghazni 1173, Peshawar 1179, the last Ghaznavid strongholds attacked in 1181 under Khusrau Malik, Lahore taken in 1186, which 'ended the Ghaznavids rule'.

wars.name: Ghurid invasion of Gujarat (Battle of Kasahrada)
wars.outcome: Ghurid army routed by Mularaja II and Rajput allies at Kasahrada; no ground taken.

wars.name: First and Second Battles of Tarain
wars.outcome: Bathinda taken 1190; Muhammad wounded in the First Battle of Tarain (1191); Prithviraj routed in 1192 and executed; Delhi and Ajmer pass to the Ghurids (Delhi directly 1193, Ajmer as a vassal).

wars.name: Battle of Chandawar
wars.outcome: Jayachandra killed; Varanasi looted and Sarnath sacked; Kannauj annexed in 1198.

wars.name: Aibak's Gujarat campaign
wars.outcome: Aibak defeats Bhima II at Sirohi and sacks Anhilwara; control did not last.

wars.name: Siege of Kalinjar
wars.outcome: Kalinjar, Mahoba and Khajuraho 'came under Ghurid control'.

wars.name: Ghurid-Khwarazmian war for Khorasan
wars.outcome: Nishapur, Merv and Tus taken 1200 and recovered by Khwarazm by 1201; Muhammad defeated at Andkhud in 1204 by the Qara Khitai and Khwarazmians and loses most of Khorasan; Herat and Balkh stay Ghurid until 1206.

wars.name: Bakhtiyar Khalji's conquest of Bihar and Bengal
wars.outcome: Bihar and the lower Ganges plain overrun; 'Islamic government' at Lakhnauti in 1205.

wars.name: Khwarazmian conquest of Ghur and Ghazni
wars.outcome: Herat and Ghor 1206, Ghazni 1215; the Ghurid rulers of 1206-1215 are Khwarazmian vassals.

certainty.note: Every Ghurid frontier is approximate: the pages name cities and campaigns, not boundaries.
